methodology: Personal multi-timeframe price action with simplified Wyckoff accumulation and distribution
objective: Test whether predetermined higher-timeframe context plus observable lower-timeframe accumulation or distribution, break of order flow, and mitigation produces positive expectancy after costs.
requirements: State the narrative timeframe, setup timeframe, execution timeframe, direction, invalidation, and target before entry.
Mark the relevant range, point of interest, and liquidity level before using them to justify an entry.
Keep chart observations separate from interpretations about accumulation, distribution, manipulation, or participant intent.
Choose one execution model before price reaches the entry: break-of-order-flow close, departure-push Fibonacci mitigation, schematic-range Fibonacci mitigation, or direct rejection.
For Fibonacci mitigation, record whether the anchors span the break-producing push or the entire schematic and whether the selected retracement is 50 or 80 percent.
Record every qualifying occurrence including valid setups that were not traded.
exclusions: Do not search progressively lower timeframes merely to find a confirming pattern.
Do not change the selected range, Fibonacci anchors, retracement level, liquidity target, stop, or setup classification after seeing the outcome.
Do not replace a missed 80 percent mitigation with a retrospective 50 percent or break-close entry.
Do not compress the structural stop solely to manufacture the minimum reward-to-risk ratio.
Do not treat a liquidity sweep, imbalance, candle pattern, or volume-profile level alone as proof of direction.
Do not combine statistics from different setup or execution types.

required: Daily and four-hour charts establish broad narrative, external ranges, supply or demand, and major objectives.
One-hour and fifteen-minute charts identify active delivery, pullbacks, continuation ranges, and setup location.
Five-minute and one-minute charts confirm and execute; they do not independently override missing higher-timeframe context.
Classify each opportunity as higher-timeframe aligned or countertrend, and as inside or outside a predetermined point of interest.
Classify liquidity separately as previous day, previous week, previous month, session, equal-level, swing, or trendline liquidity.
exclusions: No trade when the relevant timeframe hierarchy and structural invalidation cannot be stated clearly.
No countertrend trade without lower-timeframe confirmation or an explicitly separate reduced-risk direct-rejection model.

requirements: Price reaches a point of interest marked before arrival.
Accumulation or distribution contains repeated tests or drives; three drives and a final liquidity sweep increase quality but are not mandatory.
Price closes through the relevant internal swing to create a break of order flow in the intended direction.
The chosen execution model and its exact entry are recorded before the entry becomes available.
The nearest predetermined target provides at least the minimum planned reward-to-risk ratio.
exclusions: The point of interest is selected after the reaction.
The protected structural level has already invalidated.
The break of order flow exists only on an irrelevant smaller timeframe.

requirements: The higher-timeframe narrative and controlling structure support continuation.
Price retraces into a predetermined one-hour, fifteen-minute, or five-minute continuation range.
Lower-timeframe reaccumulation or redistribution produces a break of order flow in the continuation direction.
The chosen execution model and its exact entry are recorded before the entry becomes available.
No opposing point of interest blocks the minimum planned reward-to-risk target.
exclusions: The controlling protected swing has invalidated.
A small execution-timeframe shift is the only evidence against strong controlling-timeframe delivery.

requirements: Price sweeps a level marked beforehand such as a previous day, week, month, or session high or low.
Price fails to sustain acceptance beyond the swept level.
Accumulation or distribution and a break of order flow confirm the reversal.
The missing higher-timeframe point of interest is recorded and risk remains below the strategy maximum.
exclusions: The sweep alone is used as an entry.
Price accepts and consolidates beyond the swept level without a confirming reversal.

requirements: The point of interest or source range was marked before the first return.
The first mitigation produces an observable rejection candle or immediate directional displacement.
The trade is classified separately from accumulation and break-of-order-flow entries.
Reduced risk is used because the complete confirmation sequence is absent.
exclusions: Price consolidates through the point of interest.
The required stop sits inside ordinary spread or price noise.
The setup is retrospectively reclassified as a confirmed accumulation or distribution entry.
